The '''Chetaev instability theorem''' for [[dynamical system]]s states that if there exists, for the system <math>\dot{\textbf{x}} = X(\textbf{x})</math> with an [[equilibrium point]] at the origin, a continuously differentiable function V('''x''') such that
# the origin is a [[Boundary (topology)|boundary point]] of the set <math>G = \{\mathbf{x} \mid V(\mathbf{x})>0\}</math>;
# there exists a [[neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighborhood]] <math>U</math> of the origin such that <math>\dot{V}(\textbf{x})>0</math> for all <math>\mathbf{x} \in G \cap U</math>

then the origin is an unstable equilibrium point of the system.

This theorem is somewhat less restrictive than the [[Lyapunov instability theorem]]s, since a complete sphere (circle) around the origin for which <math>V</math> and <math>\dot{V}</math> both are of the same sign does not have to be produced.

It is named after [[Nicolai Gurevich Chetaev]].

== Applications ==
Chetaev instability theorem has been used to analyze the unfolding dynamics of proteins under the effect of optical tweezers.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mohammadi |first1=A. |last2=Spong |first2=Mark W. |date=2022 |title=Chetaev Instability Framework for Kinetostatic Compliance-Based Protein Unfolding |journal=IEEE Control Systems Letters |volume=6 |pages=2755–2760 |arxiv=2205.07375 |doi=10.1109/LCSYS.2022.3176433 |bibcode=2022ICSL....6.2755M |issn=2475-1456}}</ref>
